messages:
Sasha: Heads-up — after the CUDA driver push to 528.x we see a regression in short-sequence (<64) latency on the H100 pools. Profiling attached below.
Mike L: Yikes. Is this across all kernels or a specific matmul path? :eyes:
Sasha: Looks like the autotuner started preferring the 'wmma_tiled_v3' path for seq<=64 on compute capability 900 (H100). Previously it chose 'wmma_tiled_v2' which was faster for our shapes.
Jin R: Do we have perf counters? wall time diff, p50/p95?
Sasha: Quick numbers from sample trace (50k requests):
```
model: redwood-7b-v2
seq: 32
batch: 1
previous kernel (v2): p50=12.8ms p95=18.4ms
new kernel (v3): p50=18.9ms p95=32.7ms
throughput drop ~40% for small sequences
```
Alex P: That's huge. Is it the kernel implementation or a driver codegen mismatch? Could be a heuristics change in cuBLAS/cuDNN that shifts GEMM tiling choices.
Katy: We've seen similar after nvidia driver updates where autotune metrics (eg FLOP/s estimates) got skewed because of changed GPU clocks. Might be heuristics in our autotuner relying on microbenchmarks.
Mike L: Are Dedicated customers hit? We need to know impact surface.
Sasha: So far internal smoke on hosted and dedicated H100 pools in us-west1. Lower-end GPUs (A10, A100) not impacted.
deploy-bot: [CI] kernel-autotune-smoke finished — 4 failures, 11 warnings — https://ci.redwood/uid/3421
Jin R: Root cause hypothesis: post-driver, the per-shape microbenchmarks used during autotuning give noisy timings causing selector to overestimate v3 for short sequences. Two pathways: 1) rollback driver, 2) force selector hints for seq<=64 to prefer v2 until autotuner is recalibrated.
Katy: Agreed. We should mitigate with a minimal blast radius: disable autotune picks for seq<128 on H100 and fall back to pinned kernel table used before the upgrade.
Mike L: Operationally, rollback path looks heavier (driver + node reboot). Can we instead patch the runtime to short-circuit the selector for affected shapes? That can be rolled back faster.
Alex P: Patch plan: add opt-in config flag `autotune_override_shapes` that maps (arch, seq_range) -> kernel_hint. Default off. Ramp to 100% on hosted first, then dedicated.
Sasha: I'll open the PR. Quick mitigation steps I propose now: 
1) Prod: enable autotune_override_shapes for H100 with seq<=64 -> kernel v2 (hotfix)
2) Run microbench harness across driver 528.x to recalibrate autotuner for v3
3) If recalibration doesn't converge in 24h, schedule driver rollback for affected clusters (maintenance window)
Jin R: Can we also add telemetry to flag when selector changes kernel for an accepted shape? Need histograms by seq length so we can detect reversion quickly.
Sasha: Yes adding telemetry now. Patch includes metrics: selector.chosen_kernel{model,arch,seq_bucket} and a trace id for slow requests.
Mike L: For Dedicated customers with strict SLAs — should we proactively notify them about potential transient latency blips and the mitigation plan?
Katy: Yes, CS alert with A/B testing notes. I'll draft a note: what's impacted, mitigation (hotfix), ETA for recalibration or rollback.
Alex P: Rollback checklist if needed:
- schedule node maintenance window
- deploy driver 527.XX (pinned) image to pool images
- cordon & drain nodes (graceful)
- apply driver, restart kubelet, validate kernel selector unit tests
- uncordon
- run post-deploy perf smoke (automated)
- notify customers
Sasha: One more thought: KV-cache throughput seems fine, but we saw slight kvcache eviction churn during the slow traces — likely longer tokens-in-flight gives different cache pressure. Not primary cause though.
Jin R: Ok let's prioritize: hotfix selector override -> telemetry -> recalibrate autotuner -> rollback if no fix. Timebox 24 hours for autotune recal.
Sasha: Rolling the hotfix to canary now (hosted us-west1 small pool). Will post results in 30m.
oncall-bot: Oncall alerted: eng-runtime oncall is Mike L — page sent.
Mike L: I'm watching logs. If canary looks good for 30m with p95 back to ~18ms we're green.
Sasha: Canary update (30m): p50=13.1ms p95=19.0ms on canary with override. No errors. Pushing to wider pool now.
Katy: Draft customer note ready, sending to legal for minor wording check.
Alex P: After wider rollout let's run a dedicated calibration job across 10k microbench samples and update autotune DB with new latencies. Plan to keep override for 48h then re-evaluate.
Sasha: Filed follow-ups: AUTOTUNE-482 (recalibration job), ROLLBACK-93 (driver rollback playbook), HOTFIX-221 (selector override PR).
